paper.title: Generalized Lanczos method for systematic optimization of neural-network quantum states
paper.authors: Jia-Qi Wang, Rong-Qiang He, Zhong-Yi Lu

results.system_description: J₁–J₂ Heisenberg, 6 × 6 · J₂/J₁ = 0.5 · periodic · Sz = 0. H = J1 sum_<ij> S_i · S_j + J2 sum_<<ij>> S_i · S_j; spin-1/2 operators S = sigma/2; J1 = 1; J2 = 0.5; no constant shift
results.source_location: Table "Energies obtained from the NQS Lanczos method" (tab:improved_energy), L = 6, row SLL (p=0), column J2/J1 = 0.5
results.eligibility_evidence: Expectation value of H in the initial network state (SLL, p = 0) or in the optimized superposition of network states (VMCL), estimated by VMC; the SLL rows with p >= 1, which come from diagonalizing H in the span of the networks and have no error bar, and the ED and MinSR rows are other quantities.
results.notes: Spin-1/2 J1-J2 model on L x L square lattices. The boundary conditions are not stated; they are periodic: the ED energies printed in the same table are those of the 6 x 6 torus (Schulz et al.), and the 10 x 10 comparison is with the torus energy of MinSR. The sign networks are trained by supervised learning and the initial state uses the Marshall sign rule; in VMCL only the amplitude networks are optimized. The 10 x 10 SLL (p = 0) states are the aCNN states of arXiv:2308.09664 by the same authors and are recorded there.
